head: """RapidFuzz post-corrector against domain inventory.
Whisper-small with
`language='es'` will phoneticise English nouns ("Chrome" -> "Aurekrom",
"Benson Boone" -> "Benson Mould"). Re-training Whisper to handle this
is out of scope (CPU-only constraint, multi-user). Instead, we do
DETERMINISTIC fuzzy-matching of the raw Whisper output against a
finite set of known entities (apps, artists, songs, verbs).
Algorithm:
1. Tokenise the Whisper output (whitespace).
2. For each position, try 1-, 2-, and 3-gram windows.
3. For each window, RapidFuzz.process.extractOne against EVERY
category in the inventory (accent-stripped, lowercased).
4. If any match scores ≥ THRESHOLD (default 78), replace the window
with the canonical form and advance the cursor by the gram size.
5. Otherwise, keep the original token and advance by 1.
Properties:
- Deterministic: same input → same output (regression-testable).
- Bounded latency: O(N * M) where N = transcript tokens, M = inventory
size. With M < 200, runs in single-digit milliseconds.
- Conservative: keeps original token unless a CLEAR fuzzy match exists.
Lower threshold → over-correction. Higher → misses good corrections.
Inspired by commercial Alexa/Google personalized entity resolution.

head: """Auto-calibración del piso de ruido del micrófono (2026-06-07).
Problema (reporte del user): el gate de silencio usaba un umbral FIJO
(MIN_CAPTURE_RMS=350) calibrado para UN micrófono. En otro mic con más ruido de
fondo, ese 350 queda por debajo del ambiente -> el pipeline "oye voces donde no
hay" (dispara con ventilador/ruido). En un mic muy silencioso, 350 es demasiado
alto -> ignora voz tenue. Un umbral fijo NO es universal.
Solución (lo que hacen Discord/Zoom: noise-gate auto-calibrado): medir el piso de
ruido REAL de cada micrófono y poner el umbral un poco por encima. Se adapta a
cada PC sola — universal, sin hardcodear un número por hardware.
Diseño:
- El piso se estima con un PERCENTIL alto del RMS por ventana (no el máximo, que
capturaría un golpe aislado; no la media, que un pico inflaría). Robusto.
- umbral = piso × factor (factor ~2.5-3: la voz debe ser claramente más fuerte
que el ambiente). Con pisos/techos de seguridad para no quedar en 0 ni ∞.
- Re-ajuste lento (EMA) durante los silencios: si el ambiente cambia (prende el
ventilador), el piso se actualiza solo, despacio, sin que el user lo note.
Puro (sin audio I/O) para ser testeable sin micrófono. El pipeline le pasa el RMS
ya medido de cada ventana.

head: """Pure-onnxruntime LiveKit wake-word inference for Python 3.10.
The trained LiveKit model lives as 3 ONNX graphs. The
`livekit-wakeword` PyPI package requires Python 3.11, but
the Gemma 4 runtime is 3.10. This module reimplements LiveKit's
inference pipeline using ONLY onnxruntime + numpy, so it loads in 3.10.
Pipeline (mirrors livekit.wakeword.inference.WakeWordModel exactly):
audio (16 kHz, ~2 s) -> melspectrogram.onnx -> (T, 32) dB mel
-> mel/10 + 2  (openWakeWord normalization)
-> 76-frame windows, stride 8 -> embedding.onnx
-> (96,) per window
-> last 16 embeddings -> hey_gemma.onnx -> score
Models expected under models_dir:
melspectrogram.onnx   (bundled, copied from livekit package)
embedding_model.onnx  (bundled, copied from livekit package)
hey_gemma.onnx        (our trained classifier)
Threading: we cap onnxruntime to a small thread count and disable
busy-wait spinning so live mic inference does not saturate the CPU
(see scripts/_ort_throttle.py for the lesson learned during eval).

value = json.loads(path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
if not isinstance(value, dict):
raise ValueError(f"Expected a JSON object: {path}")
return value
def sha256(path: Path) -> str:
digest = hashlib.sha256()
with path.open("rb") as stream:
for chunk in iter(lambda: stream.read(1024 * 1024), b""):
digest.update(chunk)
return digest.hexdigest()
def unique_rows(
rows: list[dict[str, Any]], key: str, source: str
) -> dict[str, dict[str, Any]]:
result: dict[str, dict[str, Any]] = {}
for row in rows:
operation = row.get(key)
if not isinstance(operation, str) or not operation:
raise ValueError(f"Missing operation in {source}")
if operation in result:
